stories.headline: Reuters exclusive: Saudi Air Force conducted covert retaliatory strikes on Iran in late March
stories.summary: Reuters reported, citing two Western officials and two Iranian officials, that Saudi Arabia launched unpublicized airstrikes on Iranian territory in late March 2026 in retaliation for attacks on the kingdom during the ongoing US-Iran war. The strikes, carried out by the Saudi Air Force, mark the first known direct Saudi military action on Iranian soil. A follow-up Reuters report disclosed Saudi jets also struck Iranian-backed Shi'ite militia targets in Iraq. Both Saudi and Iranian officials declined to confirm. NYT added that UAE also conducted secret attacks.

stories.headline: Saudi FM conducts intensive diplomatic tour across Europe and Gulf amid Iran war diplomacy
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan conducted a high-tempo diplomatic campaign this week, including bilateral meetings in London (UK FM Yvette Cooper), Madrid (signed Saudi-Spanish Strategic Partnership Council MoU and visa exemption agreement), and Athens (co-chaired Saudi-Greek strategic partnership council). He held phone calls with counterparts in Iran, Pakistan, Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan, UAE, and Egypt focused on the US-Iran conflict, Hormuz shipping, and de-escalation efforts. He also met with US Special Envoy for Syria Tom Barrack in Riyadh.

stories.headline: Aramco Q1 profits surge 25% as Hormuz closure triggers historic oil supply shock
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco reported a 25-26% jump in Q1 2026 net income to approximately $33.6 billion, as the Strait of Hormuz closure drove oil prices higher and expanded refining margins. CEO Amin Nasser warned the oil market has lost more than 1 billion barrels due to Hormuz disruptions, that gasoline and jet fuel inventories are reaching critically low levels, and that market normalization may not occur until 2027 if disruptions persist. Aramco ramped its East-West pipeline to full capacity of 7 million bpd to reroute exports.

stories.headline: Aramco launches most ambitious asset monetization plan in company history, targeting $35 billion
stories.summary: Following a landmark $11 billion gas facility lease with a BlackRock-led consortium, Saudi Aramco is preparing a $35 billion asset monetization program — the most ambitious in its 93-year history — comprising sale-leaseback deals on real estate including its Dhahran headquarters campus, minority stakes in midstream/downstream facilities, and infrastructure partnerships with global investors. The company is also separately discussing raising at least $10 billion from its real estate portfolio.

stories.headline: PIF named FIFA World Cup 2026 official supporter as it simultaneously exits LIV Golf funding
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced it will serve as an official tournament supporter in North America and Asia for the FIFA World Cup 2026, incorporating Savvy Games Group and Qiddiya City. The announcement came weeks after PIF confirmed it would cease funding LIV Golf after the 2026 season — ending a ~$5 billion investment since 2022 — with PIF governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan stepping down as LIV chairman. PIF framed the World Cup deal as part of its sports priority and Vision 2030 strategy.

stories.headline: French court opens judicial investigation into MBS over Khashoggi killing following rights groups' complaint
stories.summary: A French investigating magistrate accepted a complaint filed by Trial International and Reporters Without Borders — and separately by DAWN — accusing Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman of ordering the 2018 killing of journalist Jamal Khashoggi in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. The investigation marks a significant legal development as France, where MBS visited in 2022, can assert jurisdiction. Saudi Arabia had previously been found guilty under a French criminal process and MBS acknowledged the killing was an 'enormous mistake' in a late 2025 meeting with Trump.

stories.headline: KSrelief expands Yemen humanitarian operations across health, education, and demining
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center launched several Yemen initiatives this week: Project Masam removed 839 landmines in the first week of May; an educational recovery project was launched in Aden, Lahij, and Taiz targeting 18,000+ students; a volunteer heart surgery camp funded 120 cardiac procedures in Mukalla; and KSrelief expanded cholera response, market and school rehabilitation projects. This follows Khalid bin Salman's visit to Tehran in April 2025 with a letter from King Salman, and Pakistan serving as a key mediator in US-Iran negotiations.

stories.summary: Analysis pieces this week highlighted growing fractures between Saudi Arabia and the UAE, longtime allies whose close relationship under MBS and MBZ has frayed. Disagreements span Yemen (competing proxies), economic competition, and divergent postures toward Iran and Israel during the war. Gulf policy analysts warned the US against picking sides in the rivalry.

stories.summary: King Salman issued seven royal decrees on May 15 reshuffling deputy-level posts across the National Guard, Finance, Commerce, Tourism, and the Saudi Data and AI Authority. Analysis by houseofsaud.com assessed the National Guard appointment as the most significant change, framing the decrees as a unified decision in response to the security environment created by the ongoing Iran war, including the IRGC's attempted infiltration of Kuwait's Bubiyan Island.

stories.headline: Wife of British-Saudi detainee Ahmed al-Doush appeals for release as health declines
stories.summary: The wife of Ahmed al-Doush, a British national imprisoned in Saudi Arabia since 2024 for social media posts, publicly appealed for his release as his health reportedly deteriorates sharply. The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention published a report in March 2026 recommending his release, but Saudi Arabia in April confirmed his conviction, reducing his sentence while describing the posts as terrorist-related content.

stories.summary: The Electronic Frontier Foundation launched a new advocacy campaign for Osama Khalid, a Saudi Arabian Wikipedia contributor and blogger imprisoned for his writing on Saudi Arabia, open source technology, and other topics. The EFF described the case as emblematic of the kingdom's pattern of jailing online speech.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia suspends construction of Mukaab mega-project in Riyadh amid financial pressures
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has halted construction of the Mukaab, a futuristic giant cube structure that was to be one of the world's largest buildings and a centerpiece of the New Murabba development in Riyadh. The suspension is attributed to budget constraints linked to Vision 2030 cost overruns and the financial strains of the regional war. The Spectator noted the project joins The Line as a significant MBS vanity project facing cutbacks.
